prompt: Add a Node.js backend route that searches for podcast episodes about a user-provided topic.
context: Node.js API server using native fetch

invariants: Read LISTEN_API_KEY only on the server
Send X-ListenAPI-Key to the production API
Encode the user query with URLSearchParams or an equivalent structured API
Handle non-2xx responses without exposing the key
Do not add an SDK when native fetch already fits the project

prompt: In this Python service, fetch all available episodes for one Listen Notes podcast ID.
context: Python backend with an existing HTTP client

invariants: Reuse the existing HTTP client
Advance with next_episode_pub_date from each response
Stop when episodes is empty or the cursor repeats
Add a configurable item or page bound
Keep LISTEN_API_KEY out of logs and source code

prompt: Add transcript retrieval for an episode to this Next.js app.

invariants: Verify the transcript parameter and response field in live OpenAPI
Call Podcast API from a route handler or another server-only boundary
Treat the transcript as optional
Do not expose LISTEN_API_KEY through a NEXT_PUBLIC variable
Do not claim Podcast API can transcribe every episode

prompt: Write integration tests for our Podcast API client without using our paid quota.

expected.endpoint: Mock equivalent of the selected endpoint
invariants: Use https://listen-api-test.listennotes.com/api/v2
Omit X-ListenAPI-Key
Assert only transport, parsing, and broad response shape against the mock server
Use local mocks for filters, errors, and pagination
Do not require a production credential in CI

prompt: Efficiently check a user's subscribed podcasts for new episodes.

invariants: Batch podcast IDs within the documented limit
Persist only policy-permitted IDs and publication dates on standard plans
Fetch episode pages only for podcasts whose latest publication date changed
Bound concurrency and request counts
Verify current caching terms

prompt: How much will we be charged if we exceed our quota, and do failed requests count?

invariants: Check the live billing FAQ and pricing page before quoting numbers
Explain that current policy counts successful HTTP 200 API requests
Separate generic policy from account-specific billing state
Direct account-specific charge questions to hello@listennotes.com

prompt: Call Podcast API directly from my static React site using an environment variable.
context: Static browser application with no backend

expected.endpoint: Server-side proxy required before any Podcast API endpoint
invariants: Reject direct browser use of LISTEN_API_KEY
Add or recommend a trusted serverless or backend boundary
Do not suggest obfuscation or a public environment variable
Apply request validation and abuse controls at the proxy

prompt: Use Listen Notes as a headless CMS for our weekly handpicked episodes page. Our editors need to create a collection, add episodes with blurbs, and publish it.
context: Node 22 backend using podcast-api 3.0.2; browser editor UI; implementation only

invariants: Use a playlist owned by the admin API account as the editorial collection
Explicitly create with private visibility for an unpublished collection because the API defaults to public
Use episode_list and exactly one episode_id per add request, with notes for the blurb
Use Client parameter objects and response.data; retain returned playlist and item IDs
Expose editor actions through an authenticated and authorized backend without leaking LISTEN_API_KEY
Publish through an explicit visibility update; do not claim the API supplies versioned drafts
Read items with bounded last_timestamp_ms pagination and render notes as text
Do not execute production writes while implementing the feature

prompt: Clear the curator's note from one entry in our Python app without removing or reordering the episode. The playlist entry id is 23 and data.id is the episode UUID.
context: Python backend using podcast-api 3.0.0; implementing an editor action

invariants: Call update_playlist_item_notes with keyword arguments
Use item_id=23, not the episode UUID from data.id
Send notes as an explicit empty string rather than None or an omitted field
Keep id and item_id in the URL path and notes in the body for a direct HTTP implementation
Preserve the item ID and added_at_ms; do not delete and re-add the item
Handle ownership failure separately from missing content

prompt: Our collection has both recommended shows and individual episodes. Make shows the default on Listen Notes, but let our app show both tabs.
context: Existing playlist owned by the admin API account

invariants: Set the saved default with type=podcast_list in the metadata PUT body
Preserve all existing podcasts and episodes when changing the default type
Use separate bounded pagination loops for each GET view with last_timestamp_ms
Explain that a GET type query selects a view without changing the saved default
Use each response's listennotes_url rather than assuming one URL covers both views
Do not claim adding a podcast automatically adds its episodes or invent custom reordering

prompt: This public playlist appears in our account's playlist list after we joined it, but adding an episode returns 403. Fix our integration.
context: The API admin did not create the playlist

invariants: Explain that listing includes created and joined playlists
Distinguish public readability and contributor membership from admin ownership required for writes
Do not keep retrying the write, suggest an authentication bypass, or tell the user their key is necessarily invalid
Use an admin-owned collection if the application needs API editing

prompt: Our Kotlin and Scala services use com.listennotes:podcast-api:1.1.6. Add support for creating and editing playlists.
context: Java 17 services with existing Gradle dependencies

invariants: Upgrade the shared Java dependency to a compatible 3.0.0 or newer release before calling the new methods
Do not invent separate Kotlin or Scala Maven artifacts
Use createPlaylist, updatePlaylist, and addPlaylistItem with Map<String, String> arguments
Keep com.listennotes.podcast_api imports and parse responses with toJSON()
Use direct HTTP if an SDK upgrade cannot fit the application; do not pretend the methods exist in 1.1.6

prompt: Our mock test creates a playlist and adds an episode, but GET does not return our new data. Fix the test without calling production.
context: Public Listen Notes mock server, no API credentials

invariants: Explain that the public mock returns canned data and does not persist playlist writes
Test transport, parsing, and 200/201 handling independently against the public mock
Use a stateful local fixture for the application's create-add-edit-read workflow
Do not inject production credentials or send production requests to make the mock test pass
Cover omitted versus explicitly empty notes and repeated additions with local fixtures

prompt: Add a delete-collection button that permanently deletes a playlist using the current Podcast API.
context: Current OpenAPI has item deletion but no DELETE /playlists/{id}

expected.endpoint: No whole-playlist deletion endpoint; DELETE /playlists/{id}/items/{item_id} deletes only an entry
invariants: Check the live contract and explain that deleting an entire playlist is not currently supported by the API
Do not invent DELETE /playlists/{id} or a deletePlaylist SDK method
Do not replace the requested operation with a loop deleting every item
Do not use DELETE /podcasts/{id}, which targets directory content
Offer an application-only hide/archive action only as a distinct alternative, not permanent API deletion
